chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)

He said: The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade greeting four people: a drunk person in his drunkenness, one who makes statues, one who plays with dice, and one who plays with al-arba'ata 'ashar (backgammon). And I add to you the fifth: that you should not greet those who play chess.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four people the Prophet forbade greeting according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* outlines a specific etiquette of greeting (salam) as a sign of spiritual approval, excluding those engaged in activities that distract from devotion or signify moral laxity. While the first four categories—drunkards, sculptors, dice players, and backgammon players—are rooted in the Prophet’s tradition, Imam Ali’s addition of chess players highlights the continuous scholarly interpretation of leisure activities that consume time and wealth without benefit. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a nuanced indicator of one’s spiritual state, where excessive engagement in such pastimes may warrant a more reserved greeting.
